ipatool is a command line tool that allows you to search for iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS apps on the App Store, and download .ipa or macOS .pkg app packages.

## Requirements - A supported operating system (macOS, Linux, Windows or iOS). - An Apple Account already configured to use the App Store. ## Installation ### Linux and Windows You can grab the latest version of `ipatool` from [GitHub releases](https://github.com/majd/ipatool/releases). ### macOS You can install `ipatool` using [Homebrew](https://brew.sh). ```shell $ brew install ipatool ``` ## Usage To get started, run the following command. ```text $ ipatool --help A cli tool for interacting with Apple's ipa files Usage: ipatool [command] Available Commands: auth Authenticate with the App Store completion Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell download Download iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS app packages from the App Store get-version-metadata Retrieves the metadata for a specific version of an app help Help about any command list-purchases List apps owned by the authenticated App Store account list-versions List the available versions of an App Store app mcp Serve App Store tools over MCP using stdio purchase Obtain a license for the app from the App Store search Search for iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS apps available on the App Store Flags: --format format sets output format for command; can be 'text', 'json' (default text) -h, --help help for ipatool --keychain-passphrase string passphrase for unlocking keychain --non-interactive run in non-interactive session --verbose enables verbose logs -v, --version version for ipatool Use "ipatool [command] --help" for more information about a command. ``` **Note:** the tool runs in interactive mode by default. Use the `--non-interactive` flag if running in an automated environment. ### MCP tools Run `ipatool auth login` in a terminal, then configure your MCP client to launch the stdio server: ```json { "mcpServers": { "ipatool": { "command": "ipatool", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` ## Compiling The tool can be compiled using the Go toolchain. ```shell $ go build -o ipatool ``` Unit tests can be executed with the following commands. ```shell $ go generate ./... $ go test -v ./... ``` ## License ipatool is released under the [MIT license](https://github.com/majd/ipatool/blob/main/LICENSE).
readmeHtml:
ipatool is a command line tool that allows you to search for iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS apps on the App Store, and download .ipa or macOS .pkg app packages.

Requirements

  • A supported operating system (macOS, Linux, Windows or iOS).
  • An Apple Account already configured to use the App Store.

Installation

Linux and Windows

You can grab the latest version of ipatool from GitHub releases.

macOS

You can install ipatool using Homebrew.

$ brew install ipatool

Usage

To get started, run the following command.

$ ipatool --help
A cli tool for interacting with Apple's ipa files

Usage:
  ipatool [command]

Available Commands:
  auth                 Authenticate with the App Store
  completion           Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  download             Download iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS app packages from the App Store
  get-version-metadata Retrieves the metadata for a specific version of an app
  help                 Help about any command
  list-purchases       List apps owned by the authenticated App Store account
  list-versions        List the available versions of an App Store app
  mcp                  Serve App Store tools over MCP using stdio
  purchase             Obtain a license for the app from the App Store
  search               Search for iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS apps available on the App Store

Flags:
      --format format                sets output format for command; can be 'text', 'json' (default text)
  -h, --help                         help for ipatool
      --keychain-passphrase string   passphrase for unlocking keychain
      --non-interactive              run in non-interactive session
      --verbose                      enables verbose logs
  -v, --version                      version for ipatool

Use "ipatool [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Note: the tool runs in interactive mode by default. Use the --non-interactive flag if running in an automated environment.

MCP tools

Run ipatool auth login in a terminal, then configure your MCP client to launch the stdio server:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ipatool": {
      "command": "ipatool",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Compiling

The tool can be compiled using the Go toolchain.

$ go build -o ipatool

Unit tests can be executed with the following commands.

$ go generate ./...
$ go test -v ./...

License

ipatool is released under the MIT license.

releases.name: v2.8.1
releases.body:
This release adds parallel downloads and dynamic storefront discovery, and improves authentication and recovery of delisted apps.

* Added parallel download streams for large app packages.
* Added dynamic App Store storefront discovery to support regions missing from the built-in list.
* Improved recovery of previously acquired, delisted iOS apps.
* Improved sign-in errors by displaying Apple's authentication dialogs and links for required account actions.
* Reduced memory usage and startup time, with faster initial setup.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/majd/ipatool/compare/v2.8.0...v2.8.1

releases.name: v2.8.0
releases.body:
This release restores App Store authentication, modernizes store operations, and improves compatibility with delisted and legacy iOS apps.

* Restored App Store authentication with local Anisette generation and provisioning.
* Migrated store operations and signing to modern protocol.
* Fixed redownloads of previously acquired, delisted iOS apps.
* Fixed downloads of legacy iOS apps without platform declarations.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/majd/ipatool/compare/v2.7.0...v2.8.0

releases.name: v2.7.0
releases.body:
This release adds MCP integration and improves authentication, download reliability, and app version discovery.

- MCP support: exposes tools for AI agents (search, download, list-purchases, list-versions, get-version-metadata, and purchase).
- Phone-number sign-in: adds supported for phone-number login in mainland China and India.
- tvOS downloads: allows delisted tvOS apps to be downloaded by numeric app ID.
- watchOS: supports downloading standalone watchOS apps.
- Apple Arcade: supports lookups for Apple Arcade apps.
- Legacy macOS apps: supports retrieving old installer packages for macOS.
- macOS: improves support for macOS 27.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/majd/ipatool/compare/v2.6.0...v2.7.0

releases.name: v2.6.0
releases.body:
Release 2.6.0 adds macOS App Store support, builds for jailbroken iOS devices, and more reliable downloads. ✨

- macOS App Store support: Search for and download Mac apps, list available versions, and retrieve version metadata using `--platform macos`.
- Run on jailbroken iOS devices.
- Search results now show supported platforms. `list-purchases` command includes Mac apps and supports filtering with `--platform`.
- Use purchase `--app-id` to obtain an app license without looking up its bundle identifier.
- Interactive login now prompts for your email when omitted, with cleaner inline prompts and masked password input.
- Improved recovery from App Store errors and fixed issues with resuming interrupted downloads, including when progress output is disabled.
- Downloaded IPAs now include iTunes artwork when available, with fixes for OTA installation compatibility.
- Improved handling of unexpected Apple responses and fixed a Linux crash on systems with both glibc and musl installed.
- Added support for XDG_STATE_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME, with automatic migration of existing sessions when possible.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/majd/ipatool/compare/v2.5.0...v2.6.0

releases.name: v2.5.0
releases.body:
## What's Changed
* speed-up replicateZip - reduce CPU utilization and fix ZIP format errors by @jpstotz in https://github.com/majd/ipatool/pull/506
* fix: handle sap guest timeouts by @majd in https://github.com/majd/ipatool/pull/528
* fix(keychain): configure macOS credential access by @majd in https://github.com/majd/ipatool/pull/531
* add list-purchases command for owned apps by @majd in https://github.com/majd/ipatool/pull/532
* retry transient App Store authentication responses by @majd in https://github.com/majd/ipatool/pull/533
* add visionOS search and download support by @majd in https://github.com/majd/ipatool/pull/534

## New Contributors
* @jpstotz made their first contribution in https://github.com/majd/ipatool/pull/506

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/majd/ipatool/compare/v2.4.0...v2.5.0

aiSummary.oneLiner: Command-line utility for interacting with the iOS App Store and downloading app packages.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Ipatool is a command-line tool written in Swift that allows users to interact directly with the iOS App Store infrastructure. It enables the searching, purchasing, and downloading of iOS application packages (IPA files) directly to a local machine. The tool authentically communicates with Apple's servers by mimicking the requests made by the iTunes application. It handles authentication, device authorization, and secure download token generation. This provides researchers, developers, and power users with a way to archive specific versions of applications or analyze application binaries.
keyFeatures: App Store search capability: Queries the iOS App Store database to find specific applications by name or identifier.
Direct binary downloading: Fetches encrypted IPA files directly from Apple's servers to local storage.
Authentication handling: Manages Apple ID login and session tokens required for authorized downloads.
Command-line interface: Provides a scriptable CLI for automating application archiving workflows.
Cross-platform execution: Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows environments using pre-compiled binaries.

useCases.title: Archiving application versions
useCases.description: Download and store specific versions of iOS apps before they are updated or removed from the App Store.

useCases.title: Analyzing application binaries
useCases.description: Extract IPA files for security research, reverse engineering, or compatibility testing.

useCases.title: Managing enterprise deployments
useCases.description: Retrieve application packages for distribution via mobile device management (MDM) systems.

useCases.title: Automating app retrieval
useCases.description: Integrate IPATool into scripts to automatically download updates for specific applications.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Security researchers, iOS developers, and system administrators needing direct access to iOS application binaries. Power users wanting to maintain archives of specific App Store releases.
